cl_alc_early_drinking_later_problems.q: Does drinking at a young age lead to alcohol problems later on?
cl_alc_early_drinking_later_problems.short: Not known. Some of the link seems to come from things that lead to both.
cl_alc_early_drinking_later_problems.but: Only a few small studies followed young people over time, in the US and Norway.
how: A review found only four groups of young people whose first drink was recorded as teenagers and who were followed into adulthood.
Drinking early, rather than later, went with more drinking problems in some of them. In others the link went away once other risks, such as behaviour problems, were taken into account.
In US twins, the twin who drank without permission by about age 15 drank more as an adult than the other twin, even in identical twins. The gap was smaller than across the whole group.
In identical twins, drinking early was not clearly linked to later signs of an alcohol disorder.

cl_coc_alcohol_cannabis_couse.q: How often do people who use cocaine also drink or use cannabis?
cl_coc_alcohol_cannabis_couse.short: On average, about 3 in 4 also used alcohol, and 4 to 6 in 10 cannabis.
cl_coc_alcohol_cannabis_couse.but: These averages mix very different studies, from about 1 in 10 to nearly all.
how: A review put together 16 counts of people who used cocaine, mostly from the US.
On average, about 3 in 4 had used alcohol on the same occasion or in the same period, and 4 to 6 in 10 had used cannabis.
None of 40 recent brain-scan studies of cocaine left out people who drink or use cannabis (two left out recent cannabis use), so their results may mix up different drugs.
Animal studies almost never gave a second drug, so they did not copy how people use cocaine.

freq.what: people who used cocaine had also used alcohol on the same occasion
freq.note: Averages of 16 very different studies, 1985 to 2017, mostly US; single studies ranged from about 1 in 10 to nearly all, depending on the drug, the group and the question. The alcohol average could not be checked against the review's own table.

_tf.statement: It has been shown that drinking at a young age causes alcohol problems later.
Some of the link between early drinking and later problems seems to come from things that lead to both.
On average, about 3 in 4 people who used cocaine also used alcohol.
On average, fewer than 1 in 10 people who used cocaine also used cannabis.

_quiz.q: Has it been shown that drinking young causes alcohol problems later?
options: No, it has been ruled out

_quiz.q: On average, how many people who used cocaine also used alcohol?
